Hi Michael/Katie,

Thanks for the clear list — wanted to address each point and attach the playbook and RBAC matrix for your review. See attachments: redwood_support_access_playbook_v1.pdf (playbook) and rbac_matrix_finpay_template.xlsx (role mapping template).

Short answers up front:
- PII visibility: Support engineers operate under a scoped session context. By default, prompt payloads and request metadata are redacted when a session is initiated unless a customer explicitly enables a "full session" for debugging. We recommend submitting PII minimization rules in the RBAC template so our session UI can mask fields (we support regex-based redaction).
- Logs & retention: Redwood's hosted control plane currently stores audit logs in US regions by default; retention is configurable up to 365 days on the enterprise tier. Export formats: JSON lines, CSV. We can provide a push-to-S3 or syslog export to your SIEM.
- Residency: For strict data residency (no EU replication) we can commit to US-only control plane for Dedicated and Private. Hosted tenants can be isolated regionally on request but Dedicated is the safer SLA-backed path.
- RBAC & least-privilege: The attached matrix maps roles (Customer Admin, Support Triage, Support Full Session, Read-only Auditor) to permissions. Break-glass should be limited to a short-lived role-binding with MFA and two approvers.
- Break-glass flow: We support a time-limited token generation flow (15–90 minutes TTL), email + webhook approval options, and cryptographic audit logs for session start/end. All break-glass events are logged with operator, approver(s), justification, and automatic snapshot of the session metadata (not full payload by default).

Open items for you to confirm:
1) The exact PII fields to include in the mask list (you mentioned email, name, gov ID) — add to sheet.
2) Desired TTL for break-glass (we propose 30 minutes as default).
3) Whether you need persistent export of redacted payloads for long-term forensic use (this has cost/privacy implications).

I'll plan to walk through the playbook on Friday.

Regards,

Quick operational answers ahead of our call:
- Checkbox opt-in: yes — we can add a UI checkbox that, when enabled, allows session capture for debugging and routes captured payloads to a customer-managed S3 with encryption. By default the checkbox is off.
- For forensic reviews: recommended flow is to use session recording with field-level redaction turned on; if a deeper review is required, capture can be enabled to a customer-admin controlled bucket with a dedicated retention policy and access logs. We strongly advise pairing that with a short retention TTL and explicit legal approvals.
- Default break-glass TTL: 30 minutes. We enforce session MFA and capture approver IDs in the audit trail.
